examples.title: Wealth, health and population

examples.title: Portfolio risk and return

translationResources.title: Bubble chart
translationResources.description: Scatter charts with a third value drawn as the size of the dots: the area of a bubble is proportional to its value.

countries.title: Countries
countries.description: GDP per capita against life expectancy, the bubbles sized by population and colored by continent; valueName and format name and format the value in the tooltip.

log-scale.title: Log scale
log-scale.description: Incomes from $900 to $140k: xAxis.type: "log" spreads them evenly (×10 is the same distance anywhere) with ticks at 1, 2 and 5 of each decade. The default range snaps to the closest 1, 2 or 5 × 10^k bounds around the data ($500 to $200k) instead of whole decades; xAxis.min / max override it. Annotations and the tooltip use dollars, and onZoom reports the visible range in dollars, not in logarithms (Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel or a pinch zooms).

portfolio.title: Product portfolio
portfolio.description: Market share, market growth and revenue of the products, split in four quadrants by two reference lines; showLabels writes the names around the bubbles.

pipeline.title: Sales pipeline
pipeline.description: Open deals by days in the pipeline and win probability, sized by amount; onPointClick receives the value of the clicked bubble.

risk-matrix.title: Risk matrix
risk-matrix.description: Project risks placed by likelihood and impact on a 5 × 5 grid, sized by their cost exposure; open-ended rect annotations shade the low and high zones and renderTooltip computes the risk score.

campaigns.title: Marketing campaigns
campaigns.description: Campaigns by launch date (xAxis.type: "time") and return on ad spend, sized by budget, one series per channel; a line annotation marks the break-even and the legend items toggle the channels.

shared-scale.title: Shared size scale
shared-scale.description: Two charts compare the store regions of two years. With the same maxValue, a given revenue gets the same area in both charts; without it, each chart sizes its bubbles from its own largest value.

playback.title: Animated years
playback.description: Fertility against life expectancy from 1990 to 2025, played one year at a time with setInterval (cleared on pause and unmount). Fixed axis ranges and a constant maxValue keep the frames comparable, and a text annotation writes the year.

basic.title: Basic
basic.description: GDP per capita, life expectancy and population: the bubble areas are proportional to the populations, written with the compact units of the locale in the tooltip.
